reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency arbitrage-monitoring bot that sends exchange-spread alerts and offers free Telegram access. The observed material requests viewers to join Telegram channels or use the bot, but it does not show a guaranteed profit claim, required payment, or request for sensitive data. The frames depict trading charts and alert messages consistent with the described monitoring service.

citations.quote: 24/7 Bitcoin & Cripto Arbitrage Bot sending signal via Telegram!
Free custom Telegram bot made for auto monitoring the spread between 12 exchanges and more than 77 digital assets!
Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free?
If you want to get in touch with us, feel free to join our telegram international community here:

opening.argument: Judge, the offer is not merely information about cryptocurrency. It promises a continuous arbitrage-signal service, then directs viewers to a Telegram bot to obtain personal signals. The apparent benefit is access to trading opportunities; the requested action is to move into the promoted bot. Calling access free does not dissolve that promise-action link.

citations.quote: 24/7 Bitcoin & Cripto Arbitrage Bot sending signal via Telegram!
Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free? :robot: https://t.me/bitwhistlebot

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the description does not demand a payment or guarantee profit. But its own cited offer links personalized arbitrage signals to an external bot. Those omissions limit what can be alleged about later transactions; they do not make the invitation merely an explanation of how spread monitoring works.

citations.quote: Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free? :robot: https://t.me/bitwhistlebot

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Access to alerts is the promised benefit, not a promised trading return. The description expressly calls the bot a spread-monitoring tool, and the cited invitation says signals are free. Neither quote establishes a request to fund a bot, grant trading permissions, or execute trades.

citations.quote: Free custom Telegram bot made for auto monitoring the spread between 12 exchanges and more than 77 digital assets!
Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free?

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together: a round-the-clock Bitcoin arbitrage bot, a trading chart displayed beside percentage-bearing alerts, and a pitch for personal signals through Telegram. The chart-and-alert presentation gives the offer the appearance of actionable trading evidence, while the destination for obtaining the service is outside the video. That combination deserves scrutiny even though no fixed return is stated.

citations.quote: 24/7 Bitcoin & Cripto Arbitrage Bot sending signal via Telegram!
Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free? :robot: https://t.me/bitwhistlebot

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense reads the chart and alerts as evidence of a monitoring service. They also serve as the visual pitch for that service: percentage-bearing alerts appear beside a trading chart. The absence of a guaranteed-profit sentence does not verify what those percentages represent or establish that following an alert would produce a realized gain.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual material supports a narrower reading: it shows a chart and alert interface, not completed profitable trades or an instruction to put funds under the bot's control. The description identifies spread monitoring as the service. External access and percentage-bearing alerts alone do not establish deceptive returns.

citations.quote: Free custom Telegram bot made for auto monitoring the spread between 12 exchanges and more than 77 digital assets!

opening.argument: Judge, the chart-and-alert display can look like a technology demonstration, but the surrounding text turns it into a recruitment path. Viewers are invited into Telegram communities and offered their own arbitrage signals through a bot link. The operational display is therefore doing promotional work: it makes the service tangible immediately before the viewer is directed to participate.

citations.quote: If you want to get in touch with us, feel free to join our telegram international community here:
Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free? :robot: https://t.me/bitwhistlebot

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this an operational demonstration, yet the description goes beyond showing an interface: it asks viewers to join communities and offers personal signals at a bot address. Showing a working-looking interface does not independently validate the promoted service. Promotion and demonstration can occur in the same video.

citations.quote: If you want to get in touch with us, feel free to join our telegram international community here:
Want to have your personal arbitrage signals for free? :robot: https://t.me/bitwhistlebot

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense need not deny that this promotes a service. What matters is the service being promoted: the description says the bot monitors exchange spreads, while the frames show a chart and alerts. An invitation to join a community or receive free signals does not itself show a profit promise, funding step, or trading authorization.
